title: Through-silicon via (TSV) density and yield
bottleneck: Vertical connections through thinned silicon enable 3D stacking, but TSVs have hard limits: aspect ratios cap how thin wafers can be drilled and filled, keep-out zones waste silicon area, and thermo-mechanical stress from copper TSVs cracks nearby transistors. Filling millions of deep vias without voids at high throughput is a yield challenge, and TSV capacitance adds signal and power penalties.
why_it_blocks: TSV density sets how much bandwidth can move between stacked dies; insufficient density forces architects to keep data movement shallow, limiting 3D stacking to memory-on-logic rather than true logic-on-logic integration. Yield loss from TSV defects compounds across every stacked layer.
current_state: TSVs are in volume production for HBM memory stacks and image sensors, with aspect ratios and pitches improving incrementally. Logic-on-logic TSV stacks remain rare outside flagship products due to cost and thermal constraints.
